To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose a version of constrained spectral clustering which incorporates the fairness notion proposed in (Chierichetti et.al, 2017), and (b) we provide rigorous theoretical results on the performance of these algorithms on a natural generalization of the stochastic blockmodel where groups have a "natural" fair structure.

(i) we develop variants of spectral clustering algorithms which help find fairer solutions on both synthetic and benchmark datasets and (ii) we provide theoretical guarantees for these algorithms on a variant of the stochastic model with strong inter-group connectivity.
we provide the first rigorous theoretical guarantees for constrained spectral clustering algorithms, and that these algorithms can be used to recover fair clustering in stochastic block models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new algorithms and theoretical results for constrained SC with fairness constraints.
the following question: can we develop a clustering framework that is both fair and efficient?

the following questions: (i) Can we develop a spectral clustering algorithm that is fair? (ii) Can we theoretically justify the fairness of the resulting partition? (iii) Can we provide experimental evidence of the fairness of our approach?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed new algorithms for fair spectral clustering, that are theoretically justified, and which are empirically effective in finding fair clusters.

the algorithms proposed by the authors can be used to find fairer clusterizations on synthetic and real data, and the theoretical results show that they can recover fair clusterings in the stochastic block model.
our proposed algorithms provide a principled and effective approach for fair SC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the first time, we provide a rigorous analysis of a constrained SC method which is able to find fair clusterings on a stochastic block model.
we propose a general framework of incorporating the fairness notion of Chierichetti, et al. (NIPS 2017) in the context of SC and provide theoretical and experimental guarantees for our algorithms.
, given a dataset with a fair natural clustering structure, our algorithms can recover it, even when there is no guarantee that the natural clusters have strong inter-cluster connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
incorporating fairness constraints can help in the design of better spectral algorithms.
fairness can be achieved in the context of SC, without compromising the quality of the clustering.
fairness and accuracy can go hand in hand, even in challenging situations where the data does not exhibit a natural clustering structure.
